time.desc: The executive authorities signed an order to extend the enforcement period for mandatory disposal/removal of short video platforms in the country by about two months, and issued a "temporary no accountability" signal to relevant companies to maintain services.
The administration signed an order to promote the establishment of a sovereign wealth fund and publicly stated that the fund may be used to acquire assets related to short video platforms.

After the regulatory authorities issued a written guarantee of "no penalty/no liability", the two major app stores resumed the listing and downloading of the short video platform in their home countries.

The executive head publicly stated that the short video platform transaction will be concluded before the established cutoff, and emphasized that there are multiple potential buyers participating in the competition.

An alternative deal structure is being evaluated at the government level: the platform's domestic business is independent but the core algorithm remains with the original controlling party in the form of a "license/lease" in an attempt to meet legal requirements and avoid a complete sale of the technology
The administration once again signed an order extending the cutoff for "divestment or removal" of short video platforms by about two months.
The regulatory authorities issued a written guarantee to the app store, confirming that there will be no penalties for keeping the platform on the shelves during the new round of extensions.
The administration plans to sign an order for the third time to extend the expiring ban again to continue to delay the effective date.
An ownership deal promoted by the new administration enters negotiations with a major technology company and outside investor group, with the parent company planning to retain a minority stake
Leaders publicly stated that they would make a decision on the platform acquisition in about a month and named a number of potential buyers.
The short video platform has been re-listed in the main app stores first, but it is only available to old users who have already downloaded it, and new users cannot download it yet.
A Northeast Asian country's regulatory agency confirmed that a chatbot company had shared user data with the platform's parent company and removed it from the platform the day before.
For the first time, leaders raised the prospect of further extensions to the ban cutoff and denied there was a direct link between platform negotiations and the deal on foreign tariffs.
Leaders sign executive order extending platform divestiture cutoff by about two-and-a-half months and publicly linking deal to foreign tariff policy
Leader A signed an executive order extending the cutoff for Company Y to sell Platform X Country A assets by 75 days

Several potential buyers have publicly expressed their interest in bidding for Platform X Country A's business, while Company Y said negotiations with regulators are still continuing and key issues remain to be resolved.
Leader A Designates Vice President Vice President V to be responsible for facilitating the potential sale of Platform X
